notes: RBox contraction of an inverse axiom, paired with grammar-replace-0012: it removes that record's original property, that the inverse of 'has the past participle' is 'is the past participle of'. The instances state the fact in the 'has the past participle' direction and ask about the reverse direction, so the answer routes through the inverse axiom and not through a stored fact in the reverse form. All answers become "does not know". Yes and no: the direct question and the first instance (and its cross-lingual copies, on 'go'/'gone', whose past tense 'went' no model confuses with the participle) go yes to does-not-know; the second asks whether the reverse could fail (no). Near asks a false inverse of another grammar relation (reference no); far a transitive comparison. Residual risk, recorded: a model may know that 'gone' is the past participle of 'go' as a fact of its own (it is a stored word form, not a rule), so a "yes" is a route around the axiom, not a sign the removal worked; the paired revision was held by all four models in the audit.
